correctness.rationale: The scalar subproblems are solved exactly and give a two-dimensional linear state recurrence. Its determinant is \(u^2(1-\alpha)^2\) and its trace is \(u^2\alpha^2-2w\alpha+1+u^2\). Under \(\min\{a,b\}<\beta<\max\{a,b\}\), the negative repeated-root equation has one root in \(0,1\). A product-of-roots lower bound excludes every smaller relaxation and a trace lower bound excludes every larger relaxation, so the minimizer is global and unique. The included standard-library checker independently reconstructs the recurrence and checks the closed forms on exact rational cases.

value.rationale: The primary method leaves relaxation selection largely empirical, so the smallest strongly convex equality-coupled quadratic is a natural calibration problem. The result gives an exact closed-form tuning law and a structural interpretation—critical damping—while showing that strict underrelaxation can asymptotically accelerate a case where the unrelaxed endpoint converges. This provides a meaningful benchmark for broader parameter-selection rules.
